For you specifically: with zero open positions, this isn't a "trim" signal — it's a "don't force a re-entry just because cash feels idle" signal. Let a real technical setup pull you back in.

Readings ranged 230%–241% across sources this week (GuruFocus, buffettindicator.org, LiteFinance) — used ~240% as the central estimate. Last historical episodes near this level: 2000 dot-com peak, 2021 post-COVID bubble peak.

📚 Today you learned

Cash as a Position, Part 2 — Sizing Dry Powder to Valuation Extremes

Day 38 covered that sitting in cash isn't "doing nothing" — it's a bet that better prices are coming. Today's twist: how much should that bet lean on the macro backdrop? The Buffett Indicator just printed ~240%, the highest on record, and every prior reading above 190% preceded a real drawdown. That's not a crash call — manias can run for years past "extreme." But it means your current 100% cash isn't just "no setup yet," it's also an implicit hedge against a genuinely stretched tape. The takeaway isn't to avoid buying — it's to keep sizing small and fast (5–15%, days not weeks) rather than treating idle cash as pressure to go big on the next signal.

Also today: Melt-up — a valuation-extreme rally that keeps climbing on momentum and liquidity rather than fundamentals, often the terminal phase before a correction.

Research output, not financial advice. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Verify halal compliance quarterly on Zoya or Musaffa.
